# Phase A: static retrieval eval — semantic vs lexical vs grep on durable facts

Approved 2026-10-12 (chat). Owner: evis. Status: COMPLETE — results below.

## Results (2026-10-12)

Corpus: 255 sessions → 1,342 distilled facts (main: 878). Task set: 65
judge-refined eval-gen tasks (26 code / 22 convention / 17 concept), k=10.
n=65 undershoots the 100 target (only 65 sessions met the ≥2-facts bar) —
treat marginal p-values accordingly. Artifacts: tasks.json, a{1,2,3}-*.json,
compare-*.json in .context/semantic-eval/. Durable fact recorded:
fact:b14415c79fcc48f7298fbb76.

| Arm | useful/1k | precision | recall | latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 lexical (brain) | 1.550 | 0.111 | 0.247 | 14 ms |
| A2 semantic (brain) | 1.995 | 0.137 | 0.361 | 16 ms |
| A3 grep (markdown export) | 2.213 | 0.141 | 0.301 | 44 ms |

- A2 vs A1: +0.445 useful/1k (p=0.0007 t / 0.0002 Wilcoxon), precision and
  recall also significant → replicates 2026-06-09 ledger row. Semantic
  clears its pre-registered bars vs lexical.
- A3 vs A1: +0.663 useful/1k (p=0.0003) — naive grep significantly beats
  Brain lexical. The "A3 within 10% of A1" trigger fired with headroom.
- A3 vs A2: useful/1k and precision statistical ties (p=0.71/0.85);
  **semantic wins recall** (+0.060, raw p=0.025; low-overlap stratum
  0W/5L/25T for grep) — reachability of paraphrase facts is the one
  machinery edge that survived.
- Cost side: facts embeddings are cheap (1.7 MB vectors for 878 facts,
  +2 ms query). The expensive machinery (project-file semantic index) was
  not exercised by this phase and remains unjustified-by-default.

Verdict: embedder on facts survives Phase A on recall only; fact index vs
grep-over-export is an open question. Phase B (agentic iterative-query A/B)
decides.

## Expanded Phase A (pooled, 2026-10-12)

User asked for n>=100. entire-brain tops out at 79 refine-surviving tasks, so
a second corpus was added: marvin (103 sessions -> 376 facts -> 70 tasks).
Pooled n=149. Facts fact:b14415c79fcc48f7298fbb76 (Phase A),
fact:fff3f03d8fd0b36a40c03ffa (Phase B). Pooled results
(pooled-analysis.json):

- semantic vs lexical: +0.358 useful/1k p<0.0001; holds in low-overlap
  (+0.121, p=0.028). Replicated per-repo (entire-brain +0.445 p=0.0002;
  marvin +0.277 p=0.0006 — note marvin is under the +0.3 bar alone).
- grep vs semantic: useful/1k and precision dead ties (p=0.84/0.89);
  semantic wins recall (+0.051 p=0.0045; low-overlap +0.083 p=0.0058).
- grep vs lexical: +0.376 p<0.0001 — naive grep beats brain lexical on
  both repos.

## Phase B results (agentic A/B, 2026-10-12)

149 tasks x 2 arms, sonnet, $0.60 budget cap (0 exhausted), 0 failures.
Arms: Bash restricted to `entire brain query` vs Read/Grep/Glob over the
markdown export. Grading: fact IDs in final answer vs judge-refined gold.
NOTE: first brain-arm batch was invalid (allowedTools quoting bug denied the
tool; caught because recall was exactly 0 at turns=3) and was re-run after a
verified fix.

| Arm | recall | precision | tokens | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| brain query | 0.629 | 0.278 | 218k | $0.193 | 33s |
| grep export | 0.565 | 0.266 | 324k | $0.245 | 49s |

- Accuracy: marginal, not significant (recall p=0.071, precision p=0.051).
- Efficiency: brain decisive (+105k tokens p<0.0001, +$0.052, +16s for grep).
- Agentic grep CLOSED the paraphrase gap (low-overlap recall tie p=0.88);
  brain's edge concentrates in high-overlap tasks (p=0.0075) and the smaller
  corpus (marvin p=0.042).

## Conclusions

1. Facts semantic embedder: cheap (1.7 MB / 878 facts, +2 ms) and it is what
   makes the fact index better than grep. Keep if the index stays.
2. Brain lexical-only is strictly worse than naive grep — index-without-
   embedder is the worst configuration; do not "simplify" to it.
3. The fact index's justified value for agents is efficiency (~105k tokens,
   ~16 s per memory lookup), not accuracy. Whether that pays for the
   machinery is a product call: at ~$0.05/lookup saved, the index earns its
   keep on volume, not on quality.
4. The slow startup project-file embed was never exercised by memory recall
   in either phase. Nothing here justifies it; it needs its own experiment
   (Phase 2) or removal from the default path.

Caveats: one model (sonnet), one rep per (task,arm), silver labels, two
repos, single machine. Ledger-row draft lives here; not committed to
docs/eval_ledger.md pending user decision.

## Rank-arm follow-up (2026-10-12, fact:5b1bf196aa0d29a98ef16bbc)

Hypothesis: brain's Phase B token savings come from the ranked top-k
interface, not semantic matching. Third arm: factsearch.py — the naive
Phase A lexical scorer as a one-shot CLI over the markdown export,
brain-shaped output. 149 tasks, same protocol.

| Arm | recall | precision | tokens | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| brain query | 0.629 | 0.278 | 218k | $0.193 | 33s |
| rank CLI | 0.641 | 0.314 | 226k | $0.181 | 30s |
| grep | 0.565 | 0.266 | 324k | $0.245 | 49s |

Paired rank vs brain: recall tie (p=0.58), precision rank BETTER (+0.037,
p=0.017), tokens brain better by 3.6% (p=0.038), cost/wall rank slightly
better. Rank beats grep on every metric (all p<=0.026). Replicated
per-repo.

CONCLUSION (supersedes conclusion 3 above): the agentic value of the facts
machinery was the interface, not the matching. On these corpora the index +
embedder + RRF fusion is end-to-end replaceable by `facts files` export plus
a trivial lexical ranker. Semantic's static paraphrase-recall edge (Phase A)
did not survive agentic iteration.

## Research question

For memory recall over durable facts, does Brain's local semantic machinery
(potion-retrieval-32M + RRF fusion) retrieve the right memories materially
better than (1) Brain lexical-only and (2) plain ripgrep over
`entire brain facts files` Markdown export? If not, drop the embedder from the
facts path.

Out of scope: project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/`seed`) — Phase 2.
History already ships BM25-only (ledger 2026-06-10).

## Arms (single-shot, k=10, same task set and corpus)

- A1: `facts eval` default (lexical, no embedder)
- A2: `facts eval --semantic` (shipped model2vec RRF config)
- A3: rg runner over facts Markdown export — tokenize query, drop stopwords,
  `rg -i -c` per term, rank by summed hits, top 10, same JSON shape as
  `facts eval`. Deliberately naive: lower bound on agentic grep.

## Corpus

This repo's live brain, rebuilt: `refresh sessions` + `distill`
(agent-required; approved). Target ≥100 distilled facts; if unreachable,
stop and reassess corpus. Record corpus identity in the ledger row.

## Task set

`facts eval-gen --refine` — tasks are REAL agent queries (opening user request
per captured session); gold labels = provenance facts, judge-refined, verdicts
cached (deterministic re-runs). Stratified code/convention/howto/concept,
PLUS added lexical-overlap stratification (query↔gold-fact token overlap):
low-overlap tasks are semantic's only claimed edge.

## Metrics

useful/1k tokens (headline), precision@10, recall@10, per stratum.
Paired per-task deltas, Wilcoxon + Holm. Reference: 2026-06-09 ledger row
(+0.459 useful/1k, p=0.005, n=121). A sign flip needs investigation, not just
a report.

## Cost ledger

Embedder load time, per-fact embed time at remember, vectors store size,
cgo/no-cgo surface — vs zero for A3. Measure refresh stage durations while
rebuilding (the slow startup embed goes on record too).

## Pre-registered decision rule (user-confirmed)

- Drop embedder from facts path if A2−A1 < +0.3 useful/1k overall OR not
  Holm-significant OR not positive on the low-overlap stratum.
- Open "drop the fact index" question if A3 within 10% of A1 on useful/1k.
- Only if A2 clears all bars: proceed to Phase B (live agents, parallel runs,
  brain tools vs standard tools) before declaring the machinery justified.

## Threats

Silver (agent-judged) labels; single corpus — replicate on second repo before
any actual code removal; A3 naivety cuts one way (grep parity ⇒ a fortiori;
grep loss ⇒ Phase B still required).

content.text:
# Full matrix results — the answer is "it depends on model strength and corpus size," with sharp boundaries

**1,311 agent runs, $280 total.** Mean recall per cell (significance from paired Wilcooxon):

| Cell | brain | rank CLI | grep | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **sonnet**, base corpora, n=149 | .629 | .641 | .565 | brain ≈ rank (tie), both beat grep |
| **haiku 4.5**, base, n=149 | **.618** | .474 | .215 | **brain wins big** (p=0.0001 vs rank; grep collapses) |
| **fable 5**, base, n=60 | .513 | .557 | .481 | three-way tie (rank nominally top) |
| **sonnet, XL = 1,209 facts**, n=79 | **.317** | .263 | .154 | **brain leads** (p=0.07 vs rank, p=0.0001 vs grep) *and* is cheapest (256k vs 313k/575k tokens) |

Corpus-size strata (sonnet, rank vs brain): dead ties at ~20, ~300, and ~876 facts — brain's edge only appears at ~1,200. And corpus size dominates *every* tool: recall falls 0.85 → 0.35 → 0.15–0.32 as facts grow, dwarfing any tool difference.

**Storage/memory per operation** (measured, XL corpus):

| | brain hybrid | brain keyword | rank CLI | grep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| peak RSS | 316 MB | 205 MB | 14 MB | 1 MB |
| wall/query | 0.60 s | 0.53 s | 0.12 s | 0.05 s |
| disk | 19 MB store + 2.4 MB vectors (+31 MB model in binary) | 19 MB | 4.8 MB markdown | 4.8 MB |

**Bonus finding — a real bug:** the first XL brain cell was garbage because mass `promote --keep-both` queued 91,364 reconcile proposals (13.5 MB — twice the fact store), and with that backlog `query` goes silently query-blind in *all three modes*, no error. `prefer-target` is lossy even into an empty branch (114 of 876 facts survive). Recorded as `fact:fe393298…`; worth a product fix regardless of this decision.

## True determination

- **Don't remove wholesale.** The machinery demonstrably pays in two real regimes: *cheap/weak agent models* (haiku-class — exactly what you'd use for high-volume memory lookups) and *corpora ≥~1,000 facts* (where it's both most accurate and cheapest).
- **It's replaceable** for sonnet/fable-class agents on ≤900-fact corpora — which is today's typical deployment. The ranked top-k *interface* carries most of the value everywhere; embeddings add value only at the edges.
- **Actionable middle path:** keep the facts index + ranked interface; fix the proposal-queue poisoning; and weigh the 31 MB binary / 316 MB RSS footprint against a lighter lexical-default-semantic-opt-in configuration. The slow startup project-file embed remains unjustified by anything measured across this entire experiment.

All artifacts in `.context/semantic-eval/` (1,311 run records, scripts, analyses), spec updated end-to-end, durable facts recorded (`fact:788fcf55…` is the determination). Remaining open calls: ledger rows for `docs/eval_ledger.md`, a bug ticket for the proposal poisoning, and whether to pursue the lexical-default config change.

import json, math, subprocess, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
from rg_eval import load_facts, tokenize, term_count
from pathlib import Path

facts = load_facts(Path('facts-export-xl/eval-xl'))
N = len(facts)
# document frequency per term (whole-word, lowercased body+paths)
import re
doc_terms = []
for f in facts:
    toks = set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9_]{2,}", (f['text']+' '+f['paths']).lower()))
    doc_terms.append(toks)
df = {}
for toks in doc_terms:
    for t in toks: df[t] = df.get(t,0)+1
avg_len = sum(len(t) for t in doc_terms)/N

def naive(q):
    terms = tokenize(q)
    scored=[]
    for f in facts:
        s=sum(1 for t in terms if term_count(t, f['text']+'\n'+f['paths']))
        n=sum(term_count(t, f['text']) for t in terms)
        if s: scored.append((-s,-n,f['id']))
    return [x[2] for x in sorted(scored)[:10]]

def bm25(q, k1=1.2, b=0.75, recency=False):
    terms = tokenize(q)
    scored=[]
    for f, toks in zip(facts, doc_terms):
        s=0.0
        for t in terms:
            if t not in toks: continue
            tf = term_count(t, f['text'])+term_count(t, f['paths'])
            idf = math.log((N - df[t] + 0.5)/(df[t] + 0.5) + 1)
            s += idf * tf*(k1+1)/(tf + k1*(1 - b + b*len(toks)/avg_len))
        if s>0: scored.append((-s, f['id']))
    return [x[1] for x in sorted(scored)[:10]]

tasks = json.loads(open('tasks-xl.json').read())
def recall_at10(ranker):
    tot=0
    for t in tasks:
        ids = ranker(t['task'])
        tot += len(set(ids)&set(t['relevant']))/len(t['relevant'])
    return tot/len(tasks)

def brain_rank(q):
    out = subprocess.run(['entire','brain','query','--json','--source','fact','--branch','eval-xl','--limit','10',q[:400]],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

            s += idf * tf*(k1+1)/(tf + k1*(1 - b + b*len(toks)/avg_len))
        if s>0: scored.append((-s, f['id']))

content.text:
Here's what the existing data says — no re-runs needed.

## What brain actually buys at ~1,200 facts

Less than the headline suggests, and not what you'd expect:

- **It is not better per-query at scale.** Static single-shot recall@10 on XL: naive rank 0.185, BM25 0.202, **brain 0.170 — last place**. The agentic win (0.317 vs 0.263) comes from somewhere else.
- The diagnosis from the run records: brain's wins concentrate on **vague, conceptual main-branch tasks** ("review all open PRs…", "what would multiplayer take…"). Each brain query returns a *different, meaning-adjacent* candidate set (the semantic arm varies with phrasing), so across an agent's 4–8 reformulations it explores a more diverse pool. The naive ranker keeps returning overlapping term-collision sets, so reformulating buys less. It's an **exploration-diversity** effect, not a ranking-quality effect.
- And keep the delta in perspective: brain-vs-rank at XL is +0.054 recall (p=0.07). The drop from *scale itself* is 0.64→0.32 for everyone. At 1,200 facts the dominant problem is corpus bloat, not ranker choice — which suggests the more valuable machinery at scale is brain's *curation* side (supersede/dedupe/distill reconcile), not its retrieval side.

## Rank-CLI upgrades that plausibly close the gap, in order

1. **IDF/BM25 weighting** — validated for free just now: +9% relative at XL statically, already above brain's single-shot. ~20 lines, no new data. This fixes my ranker's known ceiling (term collisions at scale).
2. **Expose the structure the export already has** — your "tags" exist: every fact file carries a taxonomy path, `kind` (decision/gotcha/…), and dates in frontmatter. Add `--path architecture.sync`, `--kind decision`, `--since 30d` filters. Narrow-then-rank is how agents actually beat scale, and it needs zero new infrastructure.
3. **Diversity in the top-10** — cap results at ~2 per taxonomy subtree. This directly attacks the real mechanism behind brain's XL edge (repetitive candidate pools across reformulations).
4. **Date sort alone**: weak as a default ranker (gold facts in these tasks aren't recency-biased) but worth having as a filter/tiebreak — brain itself only uses recency as a tiebreak.

The one thing that can't be verified statically is whether 1–3 close the *agentic* gap — that would be a single XL rank-arm re-run (79 runs, ~$18) with the upgraded CLI, whenever you feel like spending it. Not running it now.

So to your underlying question: at high fact counts the embedder machinery is buying ~5 points of recall and some token savings via query diversity — an effect a smarter 100-line lexical CLI with filters very plausibly replicates, while the thing that actually moves the number at scale is keeping the fact set curated and lettting agents narrow by the tags and dates you already store.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""rank2 arm: BM25-ranked search over a facts Markdown export, with filters.

Upgrades over factsearch.py (the naive rank arm):
  - BM25 scoring (IDF-weighted, tf saturation k1=1.2, length norm b=0.75)
  - --path <prefix>   filter by taxonomy path (the "tags")
  - --kind <kind>     filter by fact kind (decision, gotcha, ...)
  - --since <date>    filter by updated_at >= YYYY-MM-DD
  - --list-paths      print the taxonomy tree with counts (orientation)
Still zero machinery: stdlib only, reads the flat-file export per invocation.
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TOKEN = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9_]{2,}")
STOPWORDS = set(
    """a an and are as at be by can do does for from has have how i in is it of
    on or that the this to was we what when where which why will with you your
    our it's dont don't should would could did done about into over under""".split()
)


def tokenize(text):
    return [t for t in TOKEN.findall(text.lower()) if t not in STOPWORDS]


def load_facts(d: Path):
    facts = []
    for p in sorted(d.rglob("fact-*.md")):
        m = re.match(r"^---\n(.*?)\n---\n(.*)$", p.read_text(), re.DOTALL)
        if not m:
            continue
        meta = {}
        for line in m.group(1).splitlines():
            if ":" in line:
                k, v = line.split(":", 1)
                meta[k.strip()] = v.strip()
        if not meta.get("id"):
            continue
        text = m.group(2).strip()
        facts.append({
            "id": meta["id"], "paths": meta.get("paths", ""),
            "kind": meta.get("kind", ""), "updated_at": meta.get("updated_at", ""),
            "text": text,
            "tokens": tokenize(text + " " + meta.get("paths", "").replace(".", " ")),
        })
    return facts


def bm25_rank(facts, query, limit, k1=1.2, b=0.75):
    df = {}
    for f in facts:
        for t in set(f["tokens"]):
            df[t] = df.get(t, 0) + 1
    n = len(facts)
    avg_len = sum(len(f["tokens"]) for f in facts) / n if n else 1
    terms = tokenize(query)
    scored = []
    for f in facts:
        tf = {}

# Phase A: static retrieval eval — semantic vs lexical vs grep on durable facts

Approved 2026-10-12 (chat). Owner: evis. Status: COMPLETE — results below.

## Results (2026-10-12)

Corpus: 255 sessions → 1,342 distilled facts (main: 878). Task set: 65
judge-refined eval-gen tasks (26 code / 22 convention / 17 concept), k=10.
n=65 undershoots the 100 target (only 65 sessions met the ≥2-facts bar) —
treat marginal p-values accordingly. Artifacts: tasks.json, a{1,2,3}-*.json,
compare-*.json in .context/semantic-eval/. Durable fact recorded:
fact:b14415c79fcc48f7298fbb76.

| Arm | useful/1k | precision | recall | latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 lexical (brain) | 1.550 | 0.111 | 0.247 | 14 ms |
| A2 semantic (brain) | 1.995 | 0.137 | 0.361 | 16 ms |
| A3 grep (markdown export) | 2.213 | 0.141 | 0.301 | 44 ms |

- A2 vs A1: +0.445 useful/1k (p=0.0007 t / 0.0002 Wilcoxon), precision and
  recall also significant → replicates 2026-06-09 ledger row. Semantic
  clears its pre-registered bars vs lexical.
- A3 vs A1: +0.663 useful/1k (p=0.0003) — naive grep significantly beats
  Brain lexical. The "A3 within 10% of A1" trigger fired with headroom.
- A3 vs A2: useful/1k and precision statistical ties (p=0.71/0.85);
  **semantic wins recall** (+0.060, raw p=0.025; low-overlap stratum
  0W/5L/25T for grep) — reachability of paraphrase facts is the one
  machinery edge that survived.
- Cost side: facts embeddings are cheap (1.7 MB vectors for 878 facts,
  +2 ms query). The expensive machinery (project-file semantic index) was
  not exercised by this phase and remains unjustified-by-default.

Verdict: embedder on facts survives Phase A on recall only; fact index vs
grep-over-export is an open question. Phase B (agentic iterative-query A/B)
decides.

## Expanded Phase A (pooled, 2026-10-12)

User asked for n>=100. entire-brain tops out at 79 refine-surviving tasks, so
a second corpus was added: marvin (103 sessions -> 376 facts -> 70 tasks).
Pooled n=149. Facts fact:b14415c79fcc48f7298fbb76 (Phase A),
fact:fff3f03d8fd0b36a40c03ffa (Phase B). Pooled results
(pooled-analysis.json):

- semantic vs lexical: +0.358 useful/1k p<0.0001; holds in low-overlap
  (+0.121, p=0.028). Replicated per-repo (entire-brain +0.445 p=0.0002;
  marvin +0.277 p=0.0006 — note marvin is under the +0.3 bar alone).
- grep vs semantic: useful/1k and precision dead ties (p=0.84/0.89);
  semantic wins recall (+0.051 p=0.0045; low-overlap +0.083 p=0.0058).
- grep vs lexical: +0.376 p<0.0001 — naive grep beats brain lexical on
  both repos.

## Phase B results (agentic A/B, 2026-10-12)

149 tasks x 2 arms, sonnet, $0.60 budget cap (0 exhausted), 0 failures.
Arms: Bash restricted to `entire brain query` vs Read/Grep/Glob over the
markdown export. Grading: fact IDs in final answer vs judge-refined gold.
NOTE: first brain-arm batch was invalid (allowedTools quoting bug denied the
tool; caught because recall was exactly 0 at turns=3) and was re-run after a
verified fix.

| Arm | recall | precision | tokens | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| brain query | 0.629 | 0.278 | 218k | $0.193 | 33s |
| grep export | 0.565 | 0.266 | 324k | $0.245 | 49s |

- Accuracy: marginal, not significant (recall p=0.071, precision p=0.051).
- Efficiency: brain decisive (+105k tokens p<0.0001, +$0.052, +16s for grep).
- Agentic grep CLOSED the paraphrase gap (low-overlap recall tie p=0.88);
  brain's edge concentrates in high-overlap tasks (p=0.0075) and the smaller
  corpus (marvin p=0.042).

## Conclusions

1. Facts semantic embedder: cheap (1.7 MB / 878 facts, +2 ms) and it is what
   makes the fact index better than grep. Keep if the index stays.
2. Brain lexical-only is strictly worse than naive grep — index-without-
   embedder is the worst configuration; do not "simplify" to it.
3. The fact index's justified value for agents is efficiency (~105k tokens,
   ~16 s per memory lookup), not accuracy. Whether that pays for the
   machinery is a product call: at ~$0.05/lookup saved, the index earns its
   keep on volume, not on quality.
4. The slow startup project-file embed was never exercised by memory recall
   in either phase. Nothing here justifies it; it needs its own experiment
   (Phase 2) or removal from the default path.

Caveats: one model (sonnet), one rep per (task,arm), silver labels, two
repos, single machine. Ledger-row draft lives here; not committed to
docs/eval_ledger.md pending user decision.

## Rank-arm follow-up (2026-10-12, fact:5b1bf196aa0d29a98ef16bbc)

Hypothesis: brain's Phase B token savings come from the ranked top-k
interface, not semantic matching. Third arm: factsearch.py — the naive
Phase A lexical scorer as a one-shot CLI over the markdown export,
brain-shaped output. 149 tasks, same protocol.

| Arm | recall | precision | tokens | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| brain query | 0.629 | 0.278 | 218k | $0.193 | 33s |
| rank CLI | 0.641 | 0.314 | 226k | $0.181 | 30s |
| grep | 0.565 | 0.266 | 324k | $0.245 | 49s |

Paired rank vs brain: recall tie (p=0.58), precision rank BETTER (+0.037,
p=0.017), tokens brain better by 3.6% (p=0.038), cost/wall rank slightly
better. Rank beats grep on every metric (all p<=0.026). Replicated
per-repo.

CONCLUSION (supersedes conclusion 3 above): the agentic value of the facts
machinery was the interface, not the matching. On these corpora the index +
embedder + RRF fusion is end-to-end replaceable by `facts files` export plus
a trivial lexical ranker. Semantic's static paraphrase-recall edge (Phase A)
did not survive agentic iteration.

## Matrix sweep (2026-10-12, fact:788fcf552ff68bc5eb85aff6)

1,311 agent runs, $280. Axes: model (sonnet / haiku-4.5 / fable-5) x corpus
(per-branch tiny ~5-21 / ~300 / ~876 / XL 1,209) x arm (brain / rank / grep).
Mean recall (paired Wilcoxon markers in pooled-analysis + chat log):

| Cell | brain | rank | grep | winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet, base (149) | .629 | .641 | .565 | tie brain/rank |
| haiku, base (149) | .618 | .474 | .215 | **brain** (p=0.0001) |
| fable-5, base (60) | .513 | .557 | .481 | tie (rank nominal) |
| sonnet, XL 1209 (79) | .317 | .263 | .154 | **brain** (p=0.07 vs rank; fewest tokens, p<0.0001) |

Corpus size dominates every tool: recall ~0.85 (tiny) -> ~0.35 (876) ->
0.15-0.32 (1,209). Haiku-brain trades tokens for recall (307k vs 241k).

Resources (XL corpus): brain hybrid 316MB peak RSS / 0.6s / 19MB store +
2.4MB vectors + 31MB bundled model in binary; brain keyword 205MB; rank CLI
14MB / 0.12s / 4.8MB markdown; grep 1MB / 0.05s.

Robustness bug (fact:fe39329846002f8ba58387e1): keep-both promote at scale
queued 91,364 proposals (13.5MB > the 6.8MB fact store) and query went
silently query-blind in ALL modes; prefer-target promote is lossy even into
an empty branch (114/876). XL brain cell was re-run after truncating the
scratch proposals.ndjson.

DETERMINATION: machinery is justified for weak models (haiku-class agents)
and corpora approaching ~1,000+ facts; replaceable by export + trivial
ranker for sonnet/fable-class models on <=900-fact corpora. Recommended
action is not wholesale removal: fix the proposal bug, reconsider the
31MB/316MB footprint (lighter lexical default, semantic opt-in), and keep
the ranked top-k interface — it, not the embeddings, carries most of the
value.

## Research question

For memory recall over durable facts, does Brain's local semantic machinery
(potion-retrieval-32M + RRF fusion) retrieve the right memories materially
better than (1) Brain lexical-only and (2) plain ripgrep over
`entire brain facts files` Markdown export? If not, drop the embedder from the
facts path.

Out of scope: project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/`seed`) — Phase 2.
History already ships BM25-only (ledger 2026-06-10).

## Arms (single-shot, k=10, same task set and corpus)

- A1: `facts eval` default (lexical, no embedder)
- A2: `facts eval --semantic` (shipped model2vec RRF config)
- A3: rg runner over facts Markdown export — tokenize query, drop stopwords,
  `rg -i -c` per term, rank by summed hits, top 10, same JSON shape as
  `facts eval`. Deliberately naive: lower bound on agentic grep.

## Corpus

This repo's live brain, rebuilt: `refresh sessions` + `distill`
(agent-required; approved). Target ≥100 distilled facts; if unreachable,
stop and reassess corpus. Record corpus identity in the ledger row.

## Task set

`facts eval-gen --refine` — tasks are REAL agent queries (opening user request
per captured session); gold labels = provenance facts, judge-refined, verdicts
cached (deterministic re-runs). Stratified code/convention/howto/concept,
PLUS added lexical-overlap stratification (query↔gold-fact token overlap):
low-overlap tasks are semantic's only claimed edge.

## Metrics

useful/1k tokens (headline), precision@10, recall@10, per stratum.
Paired per-task deltas, Wilcoxon + Holm. Reference: 2026-06-09 ledger row
(+0.459 useful/1k, p=0.005, n=121). A sign flip needs investigation, not just
a report.

## Cost ledger

Embedder load time, per-fact embed time at remember, vectors store size,
cgo/no-cgo surface — vs zero for A3. Measure refresh stage durations while
rebuilding (the slow startup embed goes on record too).

## Pre-registered decision rule (user-confirmed)

- Drop embedder from facts path if A2−A1 < +0.3 useful/1k overall OR not
  Holm-significant OR not positive on the low-overlap stratum.
- Open "drop the fact index" question if A3 within 10% of A1 on useful/1k.
- Only if A2 clears all bars: proceed to Phase B (live agents, parallel runs,
  brain tools vs standard tools) before declaring the machinery justified.

## Threats

Silver (agent-judged) labels; single corpus — replicate on second repo before
any actual code removal; A3 naivety cuts one way (grep parity ⇒ a fortiori;
grep loss ⇒ Phase B still required).

**The upgraded CLI matches or beats the full semantic stack in every cell.** Mean recall, all four methods:

| Cell | semantic (brain) | rank CLI | grep | **rank2 (BM25+filters)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet, base (n=149) | .629 | .641 | .565 | **.692** |
| haiku 4.5, base (n=149) | **.618** | .474 | .215 | .563 |
| fable 5, base (n=60) | .513 | .557 | .481 | **.595** |

- **sonnet**: rank2 significantly better on recall (p=0.022) *and* precision (p=0.006), with **28% fewer tokens** (157k vs 218k, p<0.0001) and the fewest turns (6.5).

# Proposal: replace Brain's semantic facts retrieval with an in-process BM25 ranker

**Ask:** approve replacing the facts-path semantic machinery (bundled 31 MB
Model2Vec embedder, per-branch vector stores, RRF fusion, sqlite-vec cgo
variant) with a ~200-line in-process BM25 ranker plus taxonomy/kind/date
filters over the existing fact store. Semantic becomes opt-in or is deleted.

**Evidence:** 1,748 live agent runs (~$365), two repos, three models, four
corpus sizes, deterministic gold-label grading. Artifacts and all run records
in `.context/semantic-eval/` on branch `brain-semantic-search-eval`; durable
facts fact:788fcf55…, fact:fe393298…, fact:55e75df2….

## Why we ran this

Brain carries heavy machinery whose value was unmeasured end-to-end: a
bundled embedding model in every binary, vector caches, fusion ranking, and
a cgo build variant. The ledger's prior evidence (2026-06) showed semantic
fusion beat Brain's own lexical mode on static ranking metrics — but never
tested the real question: **does an agent, which can reformulate queries,
find the right memories with simpler tools just as well?**

## Method (why these numbers are trustworthy)

- **Tasks:** 149 real agent queries — each is the opening user request of a
  captured session on entire-brain (79) or marvin (70). Gold labels are the
  facts distilled from that session, judge-refined, fixed before any arm ran.
- **Corpora:** rebuilt live brains — 255 sessions → 1,342 facts
  (entire-brain), 103 → 376 (marvin); plus a 1,209-fact merged corpus (XL)
  for the scale test. Per-branch slices give ~5–900-fact sizes.
- **Design:** one live Claude Code agent per (task, arm, model), identical
  prompt and budget, the ONLY difference being the search tool available.
  Paired per-task comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank. Grading is deterministic
  (fact IDs in the final answer vs gold).
- **Arms:**
  1. `brain query` — the shipped hybrid retrieval (lexical + embeddings, RRF)
  2. `rank` — naive term-match CLI over `facts files` Markdown export
  3. `grep` — Read/Grep/Glob over the same export
  4. `rank2` — BM25 + `--path/--kind/--since` filters + `--list-paths`
     (the proposed replacement, as a Python prototype)

## Results

### Agent recall (did the agent surface the right memories?)

| Cell | brain (semantic) | rank2 (proposed) | significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet, base corpora, n=149 | .629 | **.692** | rank2 better, p=0.022 |
| fable 5, base, n=60 | .513 | **.595** | rank2 ahead, p=0.07 |
| sonnet, 1,209-fact corpus, n=79 | .317 | **.326** | tie (p=0.88) |
| haiku 4.5, base, n=149 | **.618** | .563 | brain marginal, p=0.051 |

Precision: rank2 significantly better on sonnet (p=0.006), tied elsewhere.
Naive grep is not the proposal — it loses badly on weak models (.215) and
at scale (.154). The proposal is the ranked top-k interface with BM25.

### Agent cost (tokens per memory-retrieval task, same answers)

| Cell | brain | rank2 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet base | 218k | **157k** | −28%, p<0.0001 |
| haiku base | 307k | **251k** | −18%, p<0.0001 |
| fable base | 194k | **180k** | n.s. |
| sonnet XL | 256k | **203k** | −20%, p<0.0001 |

### Machine cost (measured, 1,209-fact corpus)

| | brain hybrid | rank2 equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| peak RSS per query | 316 MB (205 MB keyword — embedder adds ~111 MB) | 14 MB |
| wall per query | 0.60 s | 0.12 s |
| disk | 19 MB store + 2.4 MB vectors + **31 MB model in every binary** | 4.8 MB flat files |
| build surface | cgo variant exists for sqlite-vec KNN | pure Go |

### What semantic actually bought, isolated

- Static (single-shot) ranking: semantic beats Brain's lexical mode
  (+0.36 useful/1k, p<0.0001 — consistent with the 2026-06 ledger row), but
  **a naive grep script also beats Brain's lexical mode** (p=0.0003), and
  BM25 beats semantic's own single-shot at scale (.202 vs .170 recall@10).
- Agentic: semantic's paraphrase-recall edge disappears once the agent can
  reformulate (low-overlap recall tie, p=0.88). Its XL edge over the naive
  ranker was query-set diversity, which `--list-paths` + `--path` narrowing
  replicates.

## Bugs found along the way (fix regardless of decision)

1. **Proposal-queue poisoning:** with a large pending-proposal backlog
   (91,364 after mass `facts promote --keep-both`), `brain query` silently
   returns query-blind results in ALL modes — flat positional scores, gold
   facts absent for their own exact text, no error. The queue was 13.5 MB
   against 6.8 MB of facts.
2. **Lossy promote:** `facts promote --strategy prefer-target` dropped 876 →
   114 facts promoting into an EMPTY branch.

## What we are NOT claiming

- Not tested: corpora ≫1,200 facts; models outside Claude; multi-rep
  variance (1 rep per task/arm — but n=149 paired tasks per cell); the
  project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/seed — separate pipeline,
  separate decision, nothing here justifies it either).
- Labels are judge-refined silver, not human.
- The one surviving semantic edge: marginal recall on haiku-class models
  (p=0.051, precision tied, still costlier in tokens). If we ever target
  small-model agent fleets, revisit — the `Embedder` seam stays cheap to keep.

## Proposed plan

1. Port the BM25+filters ranker to Go as the default facts arm (the
   `rankFactsFused(rr=nil)` fallback seam already exists in the design).
2. Remove `assets/embedmodel.bin` (31 MB) and the static embedder from the
   default build; net ≈ −3,000 lines, −31 MB binary, −1 build variant.
3. Keep the `Embedder` interface + ollama backend only if we keep the dark
   history/conversation fusion arms; otherwise delete those too (~1,000 more
   lines — they have never passed a ship gate).
4. Migrate contracts: `--semantic` flags become no-op warnings; capabilities
   JSON reports semantic=false rather than dropping fields; supersede the
   2026-06-09 ledger row with these results; update docs/benchmarks.md.
5. File and fix the proposal-queue bug independently.

Reproduce everything: task sets, per-run records, grading and analysis
scripts are in `.context/semantic-eval/`; the harness re-runs any cell with
one command.

# Proposal: replace Brain's semantic facts retrieval with an in-process BM25 ranker

**Ask:** approve replacing the facts-path semantic machinery (bundled 31 MB
Model2Vec embedder, per-branch vector stores, RRF fusion, sqlite-vec cgo
variant) with a ~200-line in-process BM25 ranker plus taxonomy/kind/date
filters over the existing fact store. Semantic becomes opt-in or is deleted.

**Evidence:** 1,748 live agent runs (~$365), two repos, three models, four
corpus sizes, deterministic gold-label grading. Artifacts and all run records
in `.context/semantic-eval/` on branch `brain-semantic-search-eval`; durable
facts fact:788fcf55…, fact:fe393298…, fact:55e75df2….

## Why we ran this

Brain carries heavy machinery whose value was unmeasured end-to-end: a
bundled embedding model in every binary, vector caches, fusion ranking, and
a cgo build variant. The ledger's prior evidence (2026-06) showed semantic
fusion beat Brain's own lexical mode on static ranking metrics — but never
tested the real question: **does an agent, which can reformulate queries,
find the right memories with simpler tools just as well?**

## Method (why these numbers are trustworthy)

- **Tasks:** 149 real agent queries — each is the opening user request of a
  captured session on entire-brain (79) or marvin (70). Gold labels are the
  facts distilled from that session, judge-refined, fixed before any arm ran.
- **Corpora:** rebuilt live brains — 255 sessions → 1,342 facts
  (entire-brain), 103 → 376 (marvin); plus a 1,209-fact merged corpus (XL)
  for the scale test. Per-branch slices give ~5–900-fact sizes.
- **Design:** one live Claude Code agent per (task, arm, model), identical
  prompt and budget, the ONLY difference being the search tool available.
  Paired per-task comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank. Grading is deterministic
  (fact IDs in the final answer vs gold).
- **Arms:**
  1. `brain query` — the shipped hybrid retrieval (lexical + embeddings, RRF)
  2. `rank` — naive term-match CLI over `facts files` Markdown export
  3. `grep` — Read/Grep/Glob over the same export
  4. `rank2` — BM25 + `--path/--kind/--since` filters + `--list-paths`
     (the proposed replacement, as a Python prototype)

## Results

### Agent recall (did the agent surface the right memories?)

| Cell | brain (semantic) | rank2 (proposed) | significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet, base corpora, n=149 | .629 | **.692** | rank2 better, p=0.022 |
| fable 5, base, n=60 | .513 | **.595** | rank2 ahead, p=0.07 |
| sonnet, 1,209-fact corpus, n=79 | .317 | **.326** | tie (p=0.88) |
| haiku 4.5, base, n=149 | **.618** | .563 | brain marginal, p=0.051 |

Precision: rank2 significantly better on sonnet (p=0.006), tied elsewhere.
Naive grep is not the proposal — it loses badly on weak models (.215) and
at scale (.154). The proposal is the ranked top-k interface with BM25.

### Agent cost (tokens per memory-retrieval task, same answers)

| Cell | brain | rank2 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet base | 218k | **157k** | −28%, p<0.0001 |
| haiku base | 307k | **251k** | −18%, p<0.0001 |
| fable base | 194k | **180k** | n.s. |
| sonnet XL | 256k | **203k** | −20%, p<0.0001 |

### Machine cost (measured, 1,209-fact corpus)

| | brain hybrid | rank2 equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| peak RSS per query | 316 MB (205 MB keyword — embedder adds ~111 MB) | 14 MB |
| wall per query | 0.60 s | 0.12 s |
| disk | 19 MB store + 2.4 MB vectors + **31 MB model in every binary** | 4.8 MB flat files |
| build surface | cgo variant exists for sqlite-vec KNN | pure Go |

### What semantic actually bought, isolated

- Static (single-shot) ranking: semantic beats Brain's lexical mode
  (+0.36 useful/1k, p<0.0001 — consistent with the 2026-06 ledger row), but
  **a naive grep script also beats Brain's lexical mode** (p=0.0003), and
  BM25 beats semantic's own single-shot at scale (.202 vs .170 recall@10).
- Agentic: semantic's paraphrase-recall edge disappears once the agent can
  reformulate (low-overlap recall tie, p=0.88). Its XL edge over the naive
  ranker was query-set diversity, which `--list-paths` + `--path` narrowing
  replicates.

## Bugs found along the way (fix regardless of decision)

1. **Proposal-queue poisoning:** with a large pending-proposal backlog
   (91,364 after mass `facts promote --keep-both`), `brain query` silently
   returns query-blind results in ALL modes — flat positional scores, gold
   facts absent for their own exact text, no error. The queue was 13.5 MB
   against 6.8 MB of facts.
2. **Lossy promote:** `facts promote --strategy prefer-target` dropped 876 →
   114 facts promoting into an EMPTY branch.

## What we are NOT claiming

- Not tested: corpora ≫1,200 facts; models outside Claude; multi-rep
  variance (1 rep per task/arm — but n=149 paired tasks per cell); the
  project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/seed — separate pipeline,
  separate decision, nothing here justifies it either).
- Labels are judge-refined silver, not human.
- The one surviving semantic edge: marginal recall on haiku-class models
  (p=0.051, precision tied, still costlier in tokens). If we ever target
  small-model agent fleets, revisit — the `Embedder` seam stays cheap to keep.

## Proposed plan

1. Port the BM25+filters ranker to Go as the default facts arm (the
   `rankFactsFused(rr=nil)` fallback seam already exists in the design).
2. Remove `assets/embedmodel.bin` (31 MB) and the static embedder from the
   default build; net ≈ −3,000 lines, −31 MB binary, −1 build variant.
3. Keep the `Embedder` interface + ollama backend only if we keep the dark
   history/conversation fusion arms; otherwise delete those too (~1,000 more
   lines — they have never passed a ship gate).
4. Migrate contracts: `--semantic` flags become no-op warnings; capabilities
   JSON reports semantic=false rather than dropping fields; supersede the
   2026-06-09 ledger row with these results; update docs/benchmarks.md.
5. File and fix the proposal-queue bug independently.

Reproduce everything: task sets, per-run records, grading and analysis
scripts are in `.context/semantic-eval/`; the harness re-runs any cell with
one command.

content.text:
## 1. Does removing the facts semantic pipeline impact other parts of the plugin?

Short answer: nothing breaks functionally — the architecture already has the fallback seam — but there are three categories to handle in the PR:

**Untouched entirely:**
- The project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/`seed`) — a separate pipeline; facts recall never reads it.
- History search (ships BM25-only already), fact sync, `remember`/`distill`/`gc`/`promote`, Graph.
- The per-branch `vectors.bin` caches are documented as regenerable and never load-bearing — deletable with no migration.

**One real design decision:** the `Embedder` interface is shared with the *dark* history/conversation fusion arms (flag-gated, ollama/Gemma-based, never passed a ship gate). Either keep the interface + ollama backend for them (~250 lines retained), or delete those arms in the same PR (~1,000 more lines gone). The bundled 31 MB model is facts-only either way and goes regardless.

**Contract migrations (compiles fine, observable changes):** `--semantic` CLI flags become no-op warnings; `capabilities --json` reports `semantic: false` rather than dropping fields (committed agent-guides in user repos parse it); `recall`'s `retrieval_engine` identity string changes; the eval-harness `--semantic` arms and fusion regression tests get retired; `docs/benchmarks.md` and the eval ledger get superseding rows (the 2026-06-09 "fusion default-on" decision is reversed by this evidence, per ledger convention — superseded, not erased). One small code touch: `session_privacy_verify.go` audits vector stores as potential leak artifacts and must stop expecting them.

## 2. What is rank2, concretely?

A ranked search over the facts you already store — no model, no index, no persistent state. Four features:

1. **BM25 scoring.** Classic lexical ranking: a term that appears in few facts (rare = discriminative) weighs more than one that appears in hundreds; repeated occurrences saturate instead of dominating; long facts don't win just by being long. This is the fix for why naive matching degraded at 1,200 facts — "sync" matches 300 facts, but BM25 makes the rare term in your query decide the ordering.
2. **Filters on metadata facts already carry.** Every fact is filed under a taxonomy path (`architecture.sync.auth`), a kind (`decision`, `gotcha`, …), and timestamps. rank2 exposes them: `--path architecture.sync`, `--kind decision`, `--since 2026-09-01`.
3. **`--list-paths` orientation.** Prints the taxonomy with fact counts, so an agent's first call shows the shape of the corpus. The observed winning pattern in the runs: orient → broad query → narrow with `--path`. That narrowing loop is what replaced the exploration diversity the embeddings used to provide.
4. **Brain-shaped output.** Ranked top-10 as JSON with id, path, kind, date, and the fact text — the same one-call interface agents consumed from `brain query`, which the whole experiment showed is where most of the value lives.

How it works mechanically: load the fact records, tokenize query and facts (stopwords dropped), compute BM25 per fact over text + taxonomy terms, apply filters, emit top-k. Recomputed per invocation — at 1,209 facts that's 0.12 s and 14 MB RSS, which is why no index needs to exist. The prototype is ~160 lines of stdlib Python over the Markdown export; the production version is the same algorithm as ~200 lines of Go reading the existing fact store in-process, slotted in where the semantic reranker sits today (`rankFactsFused`'s nil-reranker path).

Both answers are now also reflected in `proposal.md` if you want them in the team doc — say so and I'll fold them in.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Proposal: replace Brain's semantic facts retrieval with an in-process BM25 ranker

**Ask:** approve replacing the facts-path semantic machinery (bundled 31 MB
Model2Vec embedder, per-branch vector stores, RRF fusion, sqlite-vec cgo
variant) with a ~200-line in-process BM25 ranker plus taxonomy/kind/date
filters over the existing fact store. Semantic becomes opt-in or is deleted.

**Evidence:** 1,748 live agent runs (~$365), two repos, three models, four
corpus sizes, deterministic gold-label grading. Artifacts and all run records
in `.context/semantic-eval/` on branch `brain-semantic-search-eval`; durable
facts fact:788fcf55…, fact:fe393298…, fact:55e75df2….

## Why we ran this

Brain carries heavy machinery whose value was unmeasured end-to-end: a
bundled embedding model in every binary, vector caches, fusion ranking, and
a cgo build variant. The ledger's prior evidence (2026-06) showed semantic
fusion beat Brain's own lexical mode on static ranking metrics — but never
tested the real question: **does an agent, which can reformulate queries,
find the right memories with simpler tools just as well?**

## Method (why these numbers are trustworthy)

- **Tasks:** 149 real agent queries — each is the opening user request of a
  captured session on entire-brain (79) or marvin (70). Gold labels are the
  facts distilled from that session, judge-refined, fixed before any arm ran.
- **Corpora:** rebuilt live brains — 255 sessions → 1,342 facts
  (entire-brain), 103 → 376 (marvin); plus a 1,209-fact merged corpus (XL)
  for the scale test. Per-branch slices give ~5–900-fact sizes.
- **Design:** one live Claude Code agent per (task, arm, model), identical
  prompt and budget, the ONLY difference being the search tool available.
  Paired per-task comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank. Grading is deterministic
  (fact IDs in the final answer vs gold).
- **Arms:**
  1. `brain query` — the shipped hybrid retrieval (lexical + embeddings, RRF)
  2. `rank` — naive term-match CLI over `facts files` Markdown export
  3. `grep` — Read/Grep/Glob over the same export
  4. `rank2` — BM25 + `--path/--kind/--since` filters + `--list-paths`
     (the proposed replacement, as a Python prototype)

## Results

### Agent recall (did the agent surface the right memories?)

Tasks = real agent queries (one paired comparison each). Runs = tasks x 4
arms, all live agents. Facts = retrieval corpus the agent searched; "base"
cells span two repos, and each task searches its own branch's slice (5-878
facts on entire-brain, ~300 on marvin; 1,718 facts total across both).

| Model | Tasks | Runs | Facts in corpus | semantic | rank2 CLI | significance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet | 149 | 596 | base (1,718 across 2 repos; per-task slice 5-878) | .629 | **.692** | rank2 better, p=0.022 |
| haiku 4.5 | 149 | 596 | base (same) | **.618** | .563 | brain marginal, p=0.051 |
| fable 5 | 60 | 240 | base (same, stratified subset) | .513 | **.595** | rank2 ahead, p=0.07 |
| sonnet | 79 | 316 | XL: 1,209 (one merged branch) | .317 | **.326** | tie (p=0.88) |

Precision: rank2 significantly better on sonnet (p=0.006), tied elsewhere.
Naive grep is not the proposal — it loses badly on weak models (.215) and
at scale (.154). The proposal is the ranked top-k interface with BM25.

### Agent cost (tokens per memory-retrieval task, same answers)

| Cell | brain | rank2 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet base | 218k | **157k** | −28%, p<0.0001 |
| haiku base | 307k | **251k** | −18%, p<0.0001 |
| fable base | 194k | **180k** | n.s. |
| sonnet XL | 256k | **203k** | −20%, p<0.0001 |

### Machine cost (measured, 1,209-fact corpus)

| | brain hybrid | rank2 equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| peak RSS per query | 316 MB (205 MB keyword — embedder adds ~111 MB) | 14 MB |
| wall per query | 0.60 s | 0.12 s |
| disk | 19 MB store + 2.4 MB vectors + **31 MB model in every binary** | 4.8 MB flat files |
| build surface | cgo variant exists for sqlite-vec KNN | pure Go |

### What semantic actually bought, isolated

- Static (single-shot) ranking: semantic beats Brain's lexical mode
  (+0.36 useful/1k, p<0.0001 — consistent with the 2026-06 ledger row), but
  **a naive grep script also beats Brain's lexical mode** (p=0.0003), and
  BM25 beats semantic's own single-shot at scale (.202 vs .170 recall@10).
- Agentic: semantic's paraphrase-recall edge disappears once the agent can
  reformulate (low-overlap recall tie, p=0.88). Its XL edge over the naive
  ranker was query-set diversity, which `--list-paths` + `--path` narrowing
  replicates.

## Bugs found along the way (fix regardless of decision)

1. **Proposal-queue poisoning:** with a large pending-proposal backlog
   (91,364 after mass `facts promote --keep-both`), `brain query` silently
   returns query-blind results in ALL modes — flat positional scores, gold
   facts absent for their own exact text, no error. The queue was 13.5 MB
   against 6.8 MB of facts.
2. **Lossy promote:** `facts promote --strategy prefer-target` dropped 876 →
   114 facts promoting into an EMPTY branch.

## What we are NOT claiming

- Not tested: corpora ≫1,200 facts; models outside Claude; multi-rep
  variance (1 rep per task/arm — but n=149 paired tasks per cell); the
  project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/seed — separate pipeline,
  separate decision, nothing here justifies it either).
- Labels are judge-refined silver, not human.
- The one surviving semantic edge: marginal recall on haiku-class models
  (p=0.051, precision tied, still costlier in tokens). If we ever target
  small-model agent fleets, revisit — the `Embedder` seam stays cheap to keep.

## Proposed plan

1. Port the BM25+filters ranker to Go as the default facts arm (the
   `rankFactsFused(rr=nil)` fallback seam already exists in the design).
2. Remove `assets/embedmodel.bin` (31 MB) and the static embedder from the
   default build; net ≈ −3,000 lines, −31 MB binary, −1 build variant.
3. Keep the `Embedder` interface + ollama backend only if we keep the dark
   history/conversation fusion arms; otherwise delete those too (~1,000 more
   lines — they have never passed a ship gate).
4. Migrate contracts: `--semantic` flags become no-op warnings; capabilities
   JSON reports semantic=false rather than dropping fields; supersede the
   2026-06-09 ledger row with these results; update docs/benchmarks.md.
5. File and fix the proposal-queue bug independently.

Reproduce everything: task sets, per-run records, grading and analysis
scripts are in `.context/semantic-eval/`; the harness re-runs any cell with
one command.

input.title: Replace facts semantic retrieval (bundled embedder + RRF) with in-process BM25 + taxonomy filters
input.body:
# Proposal

Replace the facts-path semantic machinery — the bundled 31 MB Model2Vec embedder (`assets/embedmodel.bin`), per-branch vector caches, RRF fusion, and the sqlite-vec cgo variant — with a ~200-line in-process BM25 ranker plus taxonomy/kind/date filters, slotted in at the existing `rankFactsFused(rr=nil)` seam. Semantic becomes opt-in or is deleted.

Net: ≈ −3,000 lines (+~1,260 test lines), −31 MB per binary (~47% raw, ~59% of the compressed download), −1 build variant, −~300 MB peak RSS per query.

# Evidence

1,748 live Claude Code agent runs (~$365) across two repos (entire-brain, marvin), three models, corpus sizes 5→1,209 facts. Each task is a real captured session's opening request; gold labels are that session's distilled facts, judge-refined and fixed before any arm ran. One agent per (task, arm, model), identical prompt and budget — only the search tool differed. Paired Wilcoxon per cell; deterministic grading (fact IDs in the final answer vs gold).

Arms: `brain query` (shipped hybrid = lexical + embeddings + RRF) · naive term-match CLI · grep (Read/Grep/Glob over `facts files` export) · **rank2 = BM25 + `--path/--kind/--since` filters + `--list-paths`** (the proposed replacement, tested as a Python prototype; the Go port is the same deterministic algorithm).

## Agent recall and token cost, semantic → rank2

| Model | Facts | Tasks | Recall | Tokens/task | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet | up to 878 | 149 | 0.629 → **0.692** | 218k → 157k (−28%) | rank2 better (p=0.022; precision too, p=0.006) |
| haiku 4.5 | up to 878 | 149 | **0.618** → 0.563 | 307k → 251k (−18%) | semantic marginal (p=0.051, precision tied) |
| fable 5 | up to 878 | 60 | 0.513 → **0.595** | 194k → 180k | rank2 ahead (p=0.07) |
| sonnet | 1,209 | 79 | 0.317 → **0.326** | 256k → 203k (−20%) | tie (p=0.88) |

Naive grep is NOT the proposal — it collapses on weak models (0.215) and at scale (0.154). The ranked top-k interface is load-bearing; BM25 + filters supplies it without the model.

## Resources (measured, 1,209-fact corpus)

| | semantic hybrid | rank2 prototype |
|---|---|---|
| peak RSS/query | 316 MB (embedder ≈ 111 MB of it) | 14 MB |
| latency/query | 0.60 s | 0.12 s |
| disk | 19 MB store + 2.4 MB vectors + 31 MB model/binary | 4.8 MB flat files (Go port reads the store in-process) |

## Why semantic loses its rationale

- Static ranking: semantic beats Brain's own lexical arm (+0.36 useful/1k, p<0.0001, consistent with the 2026-06-09 ledger row) — but naive grep ALSO beats Brain's lexical arm (p=0.0003), and BM25 beats semantic single-shot at scale (recall@10 0.202 vs 0.170).
- Agentic: the paraphrase-recall edge vanishes once the agent can reformulate (low-overlap stratum tie, p=0.88). Semantic's former large-corpus edge was query-set diversity, which `--list-paths` → `--path` narrowing replicates.

# Bugs found (fix regardless of this decision)

1. **Proposal-queue poisoning:** with 91,364 pending reconcile proposals (mass `facts promote --keep-both`; 13.5 MB of proposals vs 6.8 MB of facts), `brain query` silently returns query-blind results in ALL modes — flat positional scores, gold facts absent for their own exact text, no error.
2. **Lossy promote:** `facts promote --strategy prefer-target` promoted 114 of 876 facts into an EMPTY branch.

# Scope and caveats

- Known gap: marginal recall edge for semantic on haiku-class models (p=0.051, precision tied, rank2 still cheaper). The `Embedder` seam is cheap to keep as an opt-in escape hatch for small-model fleets.
- Shared plumbing decision: the dark Gemma/ollama history+conversation fusion arms use the `Embedder` interface — keep interface + ollama backend, or delete those arms (~1,000 more lines) in the same change.
- Contract migrations: `--semantic` flags → no-op warnings; `capabilities --json` reports `semantic: false` (don't drop fields — committed agent-guides parse them); `retrieval_engine` identity changes; fusion regression tests retired; eval-ledger rows superseding the 2026-06-09 fusion default-on decision; `session_privacy_verify` stops expecting vector-store artifacts.
- Not tested: corpora ≫1,200 facts, non-Claude models, multi-rep variance (1 rep/task/arm, n=149 paired per cell). Labels are judge-refined silver. The project-file semantic index (`refresh index`/`seed`) is a separate pipeline and a separate decision — nothing in this work justifies it either.

# Plan

1. Go port of BM25 + filters as the default facts arm (behind `rankFactsFused`'s existing nil-reranker seam).
2. Remove the static embedder + `assets/embedmodel.bin` from the default build; delete vector stores (documented regenerable, never load-bearing).
3. Decide the dark fusion arms (keep ollama opt-in vs delete).
4. Contract migrations + docs/benchmarks.md + ledger rows.
5. Proposal-queue bug filed and fixed independently.

# Reproducibility

Task sets, all 1,748 run records, grading/analysis scripts, and the prototype CLIs live in `.context/semantic-eval/` on branch `brain-semantic-search-eval` (workspace-local). Durable facts: fact:788fcf552ff68bc5eb85aff6 (matrix determination), fact:55e75df200666f346ff35ea3 (rank2 result), fact:fe39329846002f8ba58387e1 (proposal-queue bug). Any cell re-runs with one command via `phase_b.py`.
